primary_meaning: spiritual perception, insight, or understanding (the capacity to receive light/truth or remain in darkness)
primary_basis: Matthew 6:22-23 (eye as lamp of the body)
Mark 8:18 / Isaiah 6:9-10 (having eyes yet not seeing)
Psalm 119:18 (open my eyes that I may see)

alternatives.meaning: divine omniscience, watchfulness, or providential care (especially 'the eyes of the Lord')

notes: Biblical usage is strongly context-dependent; no single fixed symbol dominates every occurrence. Spiritual perception is the most frequently taught general association in Christian interpretation and preaching, while divine watchfulness and the evil-eye idiom are also standard. Meanings shift with whether the eye is human, divine, healthy, or evil.
